distinguishing_features: Uses pressure oscillation amplitude analysis combined with thermal imaging, rather than casing resonance frequency shift
Detects micro-scale abrasive wear via stress redistribution altering pressure wave propagation, not thermal expansion of bearing race
Threshold-based dual OR trigger (12 kPa pressure or 5°C thermal) rather than resonance-shift demodulation with load normalization
Applied to die bearing wear in extrusion, not gearbox bearing spalling
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Detect early-stage die bearing wear before it causes bar twist to exceed geometric tolerances, using existing pressure and thermal sensors.
parsed.viable_reason: The dual pressure-oscillation plus thermal-imaging approach is physically plausible at the stated scales and testable with existing infrastructure, though the magnitude derivation is heuristic.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Combining an already-recorded pressure transducer with an already-recorded IR camera to threshold-detect wear heat and pressure deviation is a routine aggregation of the closest prior art's existing-signal monitoring approach, not a non-obvious mechanism.
